publications.title: The influence of Ukraine’s State Policy on the Economy in the Modern Conditions
publications.description:
The article analyzes the influence of the state policy of Ukraine on the economy
in the modern conditions, which covers the period from 2010 to 2016. The article develops a
model of the state policy’s influence on the Ukrainian economy, which reflects the interaction
between the actors (state bodies) and the object (the economy). This interaction is realized through
measures, the implementation of which is ensured by the state policy. The work analyzes the
main economic trends, in particular, the changes in the GDP level, inflation rates, and Ukraine’s
foreign trade volume during 2010–2016. It was established that despite the 3% increase in GDP
during this period, the inflation rate rose significantly and exports reduced. The key goals for
the support and development of the Ukrainian economy at the moment include the GDP growth, promotion of private entrepreneurship development, especially as regards small and medium-
sized businesses, increase their competitiveness in international markets, which will lead to
an increase in the export volume and contribute to the decline in inflation, thereby strengthening
the national currency.

headline: AI & Data Strategy | Enterprise Transformation | People-Centric Ops | Board-Ready Executive | Speaker | Creative Achiever | Yogi
about:
I help organizations evolve, not just upgrade.

I’m an enterprise Data & AI executive embedded in consulting, operating at the intersection of strategy, advanced analytics, AI, and operating model design. I lead large, complex transformations where technology, governance, talent, and institutional purpose must move together—or not at all.

My work lives in the ampersand: where strategy & execution, data & decision-making, AI & human judgment converge. I design and lead next-generation operating models that turn ambition into durable capability: moving organizations from vision decks to AI-ready infrastructure, from fragmented initiatives to coherent enterprise systems.

I specialize in moments of inflection:
• Scaling data, analytics, and AI across regulated, mission-critical environments
• Designing target-state architectures and governance with real budget, staffing, and risk trade-offs
• Translating executive intent into executable roadmaps teams can actually deliver
• Leading workforce transitions—upskilling, role design, and performance systems—alongside technical change

What differentiates my approach is orchestration. I don’t just deliver solutions; I architect conditions for sustained performance. That means curating the right talent, sequencing decisions deliberately, and ensuring innovation emerges through design rather than heroics.

I routinely advise senior executives on data, AI, and organizational strategy; shape enterprise programs at scale; and operate with line authority over teams, budgets, and outcomes. My goal is not adoption for its own sake, but institutional learning so organizations grow more capable, resilient, and decisive over time.

If you’re leading through reinvention—whether modernizing data and AI capabilities, restructuring how value is delivered, or making high-stakes bets on the future—I’m always open to thoughtful conversation.

publications.title: The Audacity of Hype: Why International Cooperation will easily defeat Piracy in Southeast Asia
publications.description: Maritime piracy -- any non-state attack on another vessel, crew or cargo that could impede cargo delivery or crew safety -- is making news again as an "accelerating" problem in the Southeast Asian Straits of Malacca and a contained issue in East Africa off the coast of Somalia. Far from being an emergent threat, the security architecture of Southeast Asia is more than equipped to handle and prevent additional piracy operations because the specter of piracy brings even committed rivals into significant, deep and successful international cooperation on matters of security.

publications.title: What Do The Dead Say? The Architecture of Salvific Discourses in Post-Genocide Rwanda
publications.publishedAt: Journal of Power, Politics & Governance · Jun 1, 2015
publications.description: Few scholars analyze the problem of national meaning-making after mass atrocities. Whether the leaders in power after atrocity were perpetrators or not, they must simultaneously make sense of a tragic past while ruling through state institutions likely implicated in those mass atrocities. This sense-making dilemma leads to “salvific discourses”: narratives founded through memorialization of the victims of mass atrocities which produce an ongoing mythic conflict between saviors and villains that only enduring authoritarianism can contain. Analyzing “post-genocide” Rwanda, we exhume how Rwandan genocide memorials shape the remembrance of the dead and of the genocide within Rwanda. Genocide memorials, as a form of public anamnestic reasoning, create the myth of the genocidal Hutu nation by establishing the “facts” of the genocide as well as specific histories and interpretive frames for those “facts.” The facts and frames combine into “salvific discourses” justifying the practices of authoritarian rule of the Rwandan Patriotic Front (RPF)- regime: mass Hutu incarceration in the context of discredited domestic and international pressures for mass electoral participation. In other words, these memorials generate a discourse that simultaneously criminalizes all Hutu males and indicts Catholic Churches as complicit, while paradoxically positing foreign Tutsi governance as post-ethnic, salvific, and cleansing.

publications.title: Statistical Analysis of Event Data Concerning Boko Haram in Nigeria (2009-2013)
publications.publishedAt: START, University of Maryland, College Park · Jan 1, 2015
publications.description:
Using ICEWS and GTD data concerning Nigeria and Boko Haram from 2009 through 2013, this report draws on two distinct statistical methodologies to estimate which kinds of activities alter the frequency of terrorist events and which kinds of activities reduce the probability of future terrorist events. To assess the probability of future terrorist events, I simulate the effects of nine distinct scenarios to see the effect this change will have on the predicted probability of terrorist incidence in the following month.

As a result of both analyses, this report substantiates the following seven claims:

1. The triggering event that began increasing the frequency of Boko Haram's attacks is likely the jail break of September 2010 in Bauchi.
2. The largest increase in the frequency of terrorist evidence occurred in 2012. Although the
frequency was reduced somewhat in 2013, it was still above its pre‐2012 baseline.
3. In 2013, despite fewer attacks, the successful Boko Haram's terrorist incidents generate more
casualties.
4. Vigilantes have been the most effective vehicle at disrupting the ability of Boko Haram to execute terrorist attacks in successive months.
5. Military operations increased risk in Nigeria by increasing the frequency of terrorist events, as
well as the probability that an attack will happen in the following month. The more military
operations there are, the more that probability of a terrorist attack in the following month
increases.
6. Combined vigilante and military operations reduce whatever increased risk that military
operations cause concerning the probability of a terrorist attack in the following month.
7. The most effective interventions at reducing the probability of future terrorist attacks are
sustained police operations in the previous month.

headline: Director, Phoenix Multistate Tax Practice Leader at Deloitte Tax, LLP
about:
Kelley Wilson is a Director with Deloitte Tax, LLP and is the Multistate Tax Practice Leader for the Phoenix office.  Kelley brings over twenty six years of multistate tax experience serving both corporate and partnership clients across a variety of industries including: financial services, service providers, and manufacturing.  Kelley’s core background is multistate tax consulting and compliance and she is one of our MTS experts in partnership taxation serving both professional services firms as well as Investment Management industry clients.  She is also a leader in our MTS private wealth practice.  Kelley spent two years working with our National Multistate and Partnership Solutions group developing iPACS State. This development is the state tax technology and process solution to automate partnership state tax compliance and investor reporting while addressing the complexities of state and local tax compliance needs for the Investment Management space.  

Kelley previously held multiple leadership roles including the National Multistate Compliance Methodology/Standardization Team Regional Leader and Chicago office Leader, the Central Region Multistate USI Leader, the Chicago Multistate Compliance Enhancement Committee Leader, the Chicago office Multistate Tax Flowthrough team leader, and was the Midwest Region Diversity and Inclusion Leader for Tax. Within her work, Kelley brings high motivation and innovation with technology and process while delivering excellent client service. She utilizes practical solutions that add value through tax savings, time and risk management, as well as operational savings.

publications.description:
A compilation of essays and articles by important leaders in the Brazilian audiovisual industry, the book offers a panorama of the Brazilian market, including topics such as investment opportunities, content licensing, partnerships and co-productions.

Organized by Steve Solot (LATC) e Fábio Cesnik (CQS), the book also includes articles authored by Manoel Rangel (Ancine); Pola Ribeiro (SAv-MinC); Mariana Ribas (RioFilme); Paulo Sérgio Almeida (FilmeB); André Mermelstein (TelaViva); Luciane Gorgulho (BNDES); Alfredo Manevy (Spcine); and Marco Altberg (ABPITV), among others.

publications.title: A Brasil Telecom na Ponta do Lápis | Brasil Telecom: a case on telecom regulation in emerging markets
publications.description:
In 2005, the telecom regulator in Brazil asked incumbents to undertake the account separation and cost modeling. The goal was allowing the regulator to set prices based on an assessment of incumbents finance and physical data, especially the definition of cost-based prices at the wholesale market (interconnection, leased lines and unbundling prices) and the measurement of productivity to define X-factor applied to the retail tariffs in the price cap readjustment. The book describes the experience, lessons learned and process of implementing the cost models for pricing in a Major Brazilian incumbent (Brasil Telecom).

The book “Brasil Telecom: a case on telecom regulation in emerging markets”, was elaborated by nine professionals from Brasil Telecom and PricewaterhouseCoopers : Anderson Ramires, Dustin Posseti, João Alberto Santos, Jose Rogerio Vargens, Lilian Viana, Luiz Eduardo Viotti, Marcelo Henrique Padua, Rafael Guaragna Souza, Rodrigo Teixeira.

receivedRecommendations.givenAt: January 13, 2013, PJ was Björgvin Ingi’s teacher
receivedRecommendations.description:
January 3, 2013


To whom it may concern:
I am writing this letter in support of Björgvin Ingi Ólafsson’s. Björgvin was a student in my course, Social Dynamics and Networks, at the Northwestern University Kellogg School of Management in the Fall of 2011. Throughout the course, Björgvin demonstrated outstanding intelligence and drive. He often asked penetrating questions that indicated not only a deep understanding of the material, but also that he was thinking creatively about broader applications and implications of the course. 

As an example Björgvin’s hard work and ability, I can point to his final project for the course. The final project was completed in groups of four, and Björgvin took a leadership role on his team. In his project, Björgvin used social media tools to analyze the global market and competitors for an open data company which began in Iceland and is now moving to become a global data provider. He creatively discovered a way to distinguish tweets (short messages on the social media platform Twitter) by the time zone in which they were posted. Using that information, he could then understand differences in the importance of certain topics  (e.g. “Big Data” and “Open Data”) between potential European and American customers. The results were sufficiently insightful that a colleague of mine included them in a presentation at the World Economic Forum at Davos.

In my career as a teacher at Columbia University, the University of Michigan, MIT, and Kellogg, Björgvin is among the sharpest students I have encountered, and I can confidently recommend him.

Sincerely,
PJ Lamberson

featured.title: Better, faster, cheaper infrastructure with apache cloud stack and riak cs redux

slides.title: Better, faster, cheaper infrastructure with apache cloud stack and riak cs redux
slides.description:
Software is eating infrastructure.  Migrating reliability and
scalability responsibilities up the stack from specialized hardware to software, cloud orchestration platforms such as Apache CloudStack (ACS) and object stores such as Riak CS increase the utilization and density of compute and storage resources by dynamically shifting workloads based on demand. Together, these platform can saturate compute and storage of 1000s of commodity hosts with strong operational visibility and end-user self-service.

This presentation explores cloud design strategies to achieve high availability and reliability using commodity components.  It then applies these strategies using Apache CloudStack and Riak CS.

headline: Technology Strategy & Transformation Leader | C-Suite Advisor | Operating Model & AI-Enabled Reinvention
topSkills: Agile Methodologies • Product Management • Digital Transformation • Project Delivery • Project Management
about:
I’m a technology strategy and transformation leader who helps executives turn technology ambition into business reality.

Over the past 15+ years, I’ve advised senior leaders across consulting and industry on how to harness technology— including AI and emerging platforms — to reinvent operating models, drive growth, and improve execution. My work sits at the intersection of business strategy, operating model design, and technology-enabled transformation, helping organizations move from strategic intent to measurable outcomes.

I bring a dual perspective that clients value:
• Strategy consulting leadership (including senior roles at Deloitte)
• Real-world operator experience as a former founder and CEO with full P&L accountability

This combination allows me to pressure-test assumptions, validate AI-assisted analysis, and ground strategy in financial, operational, and organizational reality.

My experience includes:

Advising C-suite leaders on technology-led business strategy and operating model transformation

Developing business cases, transformation roadmaps, and value creation narratives

Guiding organizations through Plan → Transform → Scale → Run phases

Using AI tools to accelerate research, synthesis, and scenario analysis—while applying judgment to know when AI outputs are directionally useful vs. unreliable

Leading and mentoring high-performing consulting teams and future leaders

I’m known for bringing structure to ambiguity, asking the hard questions, and helping leaders make confident decisions in complex, fast-moving environments.

📍 Chicago-based | Remote-first
✈️ Open to travel
🎯 Interested in senior technology strategy and advisory roles focused on enterprise reinvention and growth

experience.description:
Hello, my name is Ashley Kailer and I’m currently a managing director with Deloitte Tax LLP.  I have more than 15 years of experience helping clients on various tax matters, including in the areas of real estate investment trusts (“REITs”), partnerships, Regulated Investment Companies (“RICs”), private foundations, and individuals. 

Specifically, I specialize in assisting clients with structuring funds for domestic investment in real estate, REIT due diligence projects, and ongoing operational tax matters.  Recently, I have significant experience helping companies understand the implications of the 2017 Tax Cut and Jobs Act.  This experience includes, but not limited to, qualified business income deduction, interest expense limitations under IRC 163(j), implications of the real property trade or business election, carried interest, like-kind exchanges, FIRPTA withholding rate changes, and modeling corporate blocker implications including the interplay with tax rate changes, interest deduction limitation, election out of interest limitation available for real property trade or business, and fully expensing.

I am married and two beautiful daughters who keep me on my toes.  I’m originally from the north suburbs of Chicago, went to college in Wisconsin, and currently live in Wheaton.

about:
Integrative, capability-building leader with over two decades of experience helping individuals, teams, and institutions navigate growth, change, and complexity. 

My career spans administrative leadership, consulting, and enterprise transformation, unified by a single focus: enabling people and organizations to perform at their best — today and into the future.

I specialize in building organizational capability at scale, integrating learning, leadership development, talent strategy, and change management into practical systems that support both strategic ambition and day-to-day execution. Senior enough to lead enterprise strategy and a trusted contributor to roll up my sleeves, I bridge vision with action, translating goals into clear structures, workflows, and development pathways that actually work.

Grounded in teaching, advising, and adult learning, I bring a people-centered, service-oriented mindset to every role. I have led programs and departments, supported diverse teams through change, and coordinated complex operations where empathy, clarity, and operational excellence must coexist. Whether supporting leaders, employees, external partners, or faculty and students, I prioritize belonging, trust, and high-quality service as foundational drivers of performance.

Over time, this philosophy has expanded through consulting engagements with mission-driven organizations including universities, public service entities, and state government departments, partnering on large-scale technology implementations, operating model redesigns, and cultural transformation efforts. I work closely with leaders to build alignment, design future-ready structures, and develop learning and change strategies that equip people with the confidence, skills, and shared understanding needed to succeed.

At my core, I am an educator at heart and a strategist by training. I thrive at the intersection of leadership, learning, and continuous improvement, designing systems and experiences that strengthen capability, enable collaboration, and produce durable outcomes.

I believe leadership is most effective when it reflects partnership, integrity, and care — values that continue to guide how I develop people, build teams, and support meaningful organizational impact.

about:
Nicola Lostumbo is an International Tax and Transfer Pricing Partner and Senior Economist at Deloitte and is based out of the firm’s Chicago office. Nicola is Deloitte's US Transfer Pricing Controversy Leader and also serves as Deloitte Transfer Pricing Life Sciences and Health Care Leader for the Americas region. Nicola has two decades of experience assisting multinational clients with their international tax and transfer pricing matters in planning, compliance, and controversy settings. Nicola's clients include leading life sciences, health care, technology, food and beverage, consumer products, and financial services multinationals. 

As Deloitte's US Transfer Pricing Controversy Leader, Nicola assists clients and clients’ counsel throughout the tax planning life cycle, and coordinates to provide the following economic support services worldwide: independent transfer pricing perspectives and analysis; audit & appeals support and data-services; and litigation support, including expert witness testimony. In his experiences, Nicola has provided litigation support to clients in US and Foreign Tax Courts as well as represented clients in numerous US and foreign tax audits, advance pricing agreements (APAs), and appeals. 

As Deloitte’s Transfer Pricing Life Sciences and Health Care leader for the Americas region, Nicola serves pharmaceutical, medical device and health care companies clients with their international tax and transfer pricing needs, including complex intangible property valuations, cost sharing arrangements, audit defense and litigations. In his role, Nicola also serves as a technical and marketing resource to the practice, coordinating globally across the Deloitte network of firms.

Nicola is active in speaking and publishing in various international tax and transfer pricing industry forums on his experiences. Nicola’s publications have examined the economic useful life of marketing intangibles, the role of intangible assets in driving firm value and profitability, as well as US corporate tax reform’s impact on US multinational competitiveness.

publications.title: The interaction of customs value and transfer pricing
publications.description: We examine how companies can manage tariff impacts on supply chains through transfer pricing and customs valuation, highlighting common challenges and strategies for mitigating related risks.

publications.title: High-value service charges and transfer pricing controversy
publications.description: We provide insights into high-value intercompany service charges, their role in creating value, and the most common tax authority challenges, before concluding with some considerations in mitigating risks.

publications.title: Business restructurings and TP controversy
publications.description:
The attention of tax authorities on supply chain reorganisations, which impact the operations of multinational enterprises (MNEs), has noticeably increased following the issuance of the OECD’s transfer pricing aspects of business restructurings (the OECD published guidance on business restructurings in draft form in 2009 and subsequently included it as final in the latest edition of the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines (TPG), issued in January 2022).

The OECD’s guidance on business restructurings is squarely aimed at analysing the impact of such reorganisations on local taxable income, outlining bases for challenges if such restructurings are deemed not to be driven by business reasons and/or (not properly documented as being) at arm’s length. The number of transfer pricing adjustments relating to business restructurings has increased significantly in recent years, and tax authorities from various jurisdictions worldwide have also become more proficient in handling such matters and have improved their technical
ability to scrutinise and challenge such restructurings.

publications.title: How are life sciences companies considering transfer pricing as they recover from the pandemic?
publications.description: The global COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted supply chains and impacted demand for therapies manufactured and sold by life sciences companies. The pandemic has also created a new layer of tax challenges for multinational companies. Many pharmaceutical and medical-device manufacturers have transfer pricing policies for the goods and services they produce and sell around the globe. In order to respond to the pandemic, recover from its effects, and prepare to thrive in the future, these organizations should consider revisiting those policies to determine how their company and affiliates may be affected.

publications.title: Global implications from digital tax proposals await the life sciences sector
publications.description: Aydin Hayri, Nicola Lostumbo, and Richard Schmidtke analyse the business model of the life sciences industry and the challenges in applying the G20/OECD’s digital tax proposals.

publications.title: Profit Splits Post-BEPS:  Quantifying an MNE's Intangibles
publications.description: A novel approach is presented based on the theory of the firm to quantify the split of profits to be allocated to the inputs of production in a transfer pricing context. In the analysis, intangible assets are shown to play an increasingly important role in explaining firm value and profitability. The econometric approach is compared and contrasted with established profit split methodologies, as well as the traditional three-factor formulary apportionment method.

publications.title: The Long-Term Effects of Advertising Expenditures: Examining the Evidence
publications.publishedAt: Bloomberg BNA Transfer Pricing Report · Dec 4, 2013
publications.description: The authors review the relevant literature on the economic useful life of marketing intangibles, specifically advertising, offering a critique of a prior article on the subject and recommending a direction to pursue in future research.

publications.title: How Much is Corporate America Worth: Corporate Tax Reform and Firm Valuation Premia
publications.description: We examine via a simple model, the interplay between current proposed tax reforms and the multinational firm valuation for foreign-incorporated firms subjected to lower tax rates on non-US income compared to the effective tax rates faced by US firms on foreign source income.

publications.title: Transfer Pricing Reforms and Tax Competitiveness
publications.description: As the US economy emerges from the most severe economic downturn in over a half century, addressing persistent annual budget deficits and a growing national debt has become a top priority for US lawmakers. One target for increased revenue is multinational companies and their transfer pricing policies, especially in the area of intangible property transfers. Given the relative fixity of capital and labor in the short term, tax reforms (such as the excess profit proposals for transfer pricing) that increase effective taxes faced by US multinational companies may bring increased revenue to the US government temporarily. Long-term effects, however, could include the loss of high-paying US jobs or potentially the eventual relocation or foreign-based acquisition of a number of US-based multinational corporations, neither of which would contribute to addressing future budget deficits and the increasing national debt that such reforms were originally intended to solve.

Using a matrix, the relationships among these factors and IS development success are logically analyzed and a model of the relationships among these factors and IS development success is proposed.

publications.title: Best Practices in Electronic Commerce
publications.description: During the late 1990s the tech bubble of the Silicon Valley grew to levels far beyond analysts’ expectations. It was believed that Electronic Commerce would be the panacea of the marketplace and that industries that implemented Electronic Commerce would reap exponential financial rewards. However, this chimerical belief was short lived and the early 2000s have led to mass re-evaluation of Electronic Commerce strategies and how they are measured. Interpretations of various factors such as brand management, channel conflict, and competitive strategies are discussed at length to serve as a best practices guide for E-commerce success.

publications.title: Improving Systems Development Through Critical Success Factors
publications.description: Presents the results of a focus group conducted to determine actions, policies, or procedures to improve the impact of specific factors that have been suggested by prior research as the most critical success factors (CSF) for information systems development. The results are based on a focus group conducted using a nominal group process. The focus group was composed of IS personnel and end-users that have had experience with systems development projects. The focus group was composed of 18 subjects from a wide variety of industries and with a diverse set of experiences with IS projects.

headline: Strategic People Partner and Culture Executive | Solving the leadership load most org charts don’t show
about:
I work with organizations where ambition is high, performance expectations are real, and leaders are carrying more than their roles formally require.

As companies grow, the most consequential people challenges rarely show up as individual skill gaps. They show up at the system level: managers absorbing program gaps, competing stakeholder priorities, misaligned expectations, and HR quietly holding equilibrium when the system is under strain. Over time, that invisible work turns into burnout, stalled execution, or cultural drift.

I partner with fast-growing organizations as a strategic people partner, helping them solve that leadership load in a way that actually gets executed — not just discussed. 

My work is designed to complement existing People, HR, and L&D functions, bringing focused, high-impact support where the pressure is most immediate.

What sets my work apart is my ability to see the system and the people inside it — to clarify and target the needs of different leaders, teams, or functions, and to bridge perspectives that are often misaligned. I’m consistently brought in to name the thing that is felt but not articulated, reframe it in a way your people can understand, and translate it into concrete shifts that generate measurable and enduring results. 

I’m especially strong in moments of disruption: new roles, first-time executives, leadership team friction, organizational change, or high-stakes stakeholder dynamics. featured.title: The World has Changed. Have Your Business Operations?
featured.subtitle: Michael Dougherty on LinkedIn

slides.title: The World has Changed. Have Your Business Operations?
slides.subtitle: Michael Dougherty on LinkedIn
slides.description: (Note: this is the first of a three-part series) With vaccines in distribution and a return to something approximating “normal” drawing closer, it’s a good time for business leaders to assess and prepare their long-term operations for the post-COVID-19 era. Many of the changes that businesses made due to safety requirements and business necessity will remain after the pandemic has passed. For example, some degree of work-from-home is likely to become a standard operating procedure for many companies, and the digital transformations that occurred were merely accelerating planned changes. These decisions will reverberate across business operations and expenditures moving forward – for example, if work-from-home becomes commonplace, what does that mean for office space requirements? How should organizations redefine the meaning of “the office”? How does it impact culture and talent development? While many businesses have already defined the necessary changes, there is still an opportunity for business leaders to optimize for this dramatically changed world so they will be poised to seize competitive advantage in the “next normal.” Here are five key areas I’m particularly focused on: Costs - Assess the real estate footprint, workforce geographic composition and desired operational scale, including areas that could be centralized to gain efficiencies. Assess fixed and variable costs and market trends to ensure flexibility and optimal cost structure. Workforce - Assess workplace changes in the next normal. What work can be done virtually and what is the impact on the workforce? Develop a point-of-view around key talent areas including safety, employee lifecycle and employee experience in the next normal. Technology - Ensure IT is aligned with business strategy and operational viability in the post-pandemic world. Consider if the business should preserve, expand or reinvent pandemic-driven digital transformations and more closely examine ways technology can enable deeper collaboration, higher productivity, and increased digitization and automation of work. Embrace movement to the cloud and technologies that enable workforce flexibility. Balance Sheet - Reassess liquidity requirements and overall capital structure to create a financially sound model that mitigates risk and enables you to act on opportunities, including investments for the recovery, despite an uncertain economy. Business Continuity - The pandemic presented unprecedented business continuity challenges. Now is the time to assess the “lessons learned” and develop a new set of recommendations and best practices for business continuity and crisis-management preparedness while continuing to monitor economic indicators and adjust actions accordingly. The first half of 2021 presents a tremendous opportunity to realign operations to align in a post-COVID world. And, unlike the “forced realignment” that took place last March, this time we can all plan strategically for a future where many of the assumptions and structures around cost, process and productivity no longer apply. In my next installment, I’ll expand on this concept by taking a deeper dive into costs and the balance sheet. In the meantime, I’d be interested in hearing what you’re doing to get ready for the “next normal.”

slides.title: Don’t Let a Good Crisis Go to Waste: Optimize Costs and the Balance Sheet
slides.subtitle: Michael Dougherty on LinkedIn
slides.description: (Note: this is the second of a four-part series) With the COVID-19 vaccine rollout underway, there’s a new sense of optimism for the global economy. As part of this, it’s time for business leaders to look at the lessons learned and investments made during the pandemic to implement revised operating models that take advantage of the people, process and technology changes that occurred during the crisis. It’s a rare opportunity to plan strategically for a future where many of the assumptions and structures around cost, process and productivity no longer apply. As Winston Churchill famously said, “Don’t let a good crisis go to waste” – so now is a great time to re-evaluate cost structures and the balance sheet. Taking Stock of Costs Cost reductions are not as simple as they may seem. They likely require corresponding investment, policy change, and change management to be successful. For many companies, office space is an obvious area for cost savings. The work-from-home requirements of the pandemic proved there may not be as much of a need for the traditional 9-to-5 office anymore. By redefining how offices are used, many companies may be able to significantly reduce real estate costs while still supporting company culture and work processes. That said, companies have to redefine policies on where people work, what kind of work can be done from home and geographic limitations due to travel or tax. And companies must account for new costs required for professionals to securely and efficiently set up home offices for remote collaboration. These decisions may even merit re-examining your location strategy. Another area to explore is travel. Since people have grown accustomed to virtual meetings and interactions over the last year, it makes sense to consider long-term travel requirements and formerly in-person experiences that can remain virtual. Again, policies need to be changed, budgets modified, and expectations set from the top to be successful in the new way of working. Re-evaluating the right mix of staff and contractors can also yield good returns in the post-pandemic world. Among the benefits of moving from fixed to variable costs is more flexibility to respond to shifting business requirements. Should you move in this direction, it will be important to assess each area and develop a workforce strategy with the adjusted goals in mind. Re-assessing cost structures should be an ongoing discipline. The post-pandemic period presents a particularly rich palate of opportunities to realign costs to a fundamentally different world. Reviewing the Balance Sheet As companies emerge from the pandemic, it’s important to assess what issues, if any, arose during the crisis with capital structure and liquidity. It’s also important to look at the road ahead and understand what the investment and capital needs are going to be, and what will be the best mix of equity and debt to finance those. Many companies discovered they weren’t properly capitalized during the pandemic, both in terms of liquidity and access to financing. The pandemic showed the value of having a strong balance sheet to protect against disruptive events and continue to make investments. The downturn provided a significant opportunity for strategic investments and inorganic acquisitions; however, many companies simply didn’t have the capital to take advantage of the situation. The recurring theme across all of this is flexibility. It reminds me of playing Monopoly with my daughter – I always remind her to have a strategy at the outset but adapt as the game changes. Not knowing each other’s approach, one of us blows up the other’s strategy very quickly by buying a property the other wanted. At that point, it’s time to throw out the playbook and create a new strategy that maps to the new reality. (And usually that’s quickly foiled, too!) The same holds true in business. It’s important to build flexibility into capital structures so you can cope with unexpected disruptions and continue to invest in the future. A global business services firm, obviously, has different challenges and opportunities than product companies and other businesses. I’d be interested to hear about how you’re looking at your business and not letting a good crisis go to waste.

projects.title: Project NEXUS
projects.description:
Design of a new public transportation system to address traffic congestion in big cities. The design covered the phases of needs analysis, concept exploration, concept definition and advanced development according to the life cycle model of systems engineering.
-------------------------------------
During this project, the basic concepts for the creation of a system of self-sufficient drones and stations in different urban and suburban areas of cities such as Houston, Los Angeles, New York or Chicago were defined. Additionally:

- System requirements were defined (IOR, TYR, PR, CR, TR, STR) at the sub-systems level (NEXUS Drones and NEXUS Stations)
- Cost structure for the elements of the system was defined.
- Different alternatives were evaluated in relation to the new technologies to be used in the system.
- The risks of the system were evaluated by performing reliability analysis and using criticality matrices.
- System Models were made using UML to represent the structure and operation of the system using IBM rational software. (Use case models, Cause-loop models, Class diagrams, Sequence diagrams, State machine diagrams, Communications / Collaborations diagrams, Component diagrams, Deployment diagrams)
- Discrete time models were developed for each of the components of the two sub-systems of Project NEXUS.

projects.title: Reliability centered maintenance plan for DISPROCAR, C.A.’s vehicle fleet.
projects.description:
This project was presented as a special degree work by both members of the team to obtain the title of industrial engineer.

This project was executed with the primary objective of designing a reliability centered maintenance plan for the meat transporting vehicle fleet at DISPROCAR, C.A. Whlist employing a descriptive and explanatory investigation, with a non-experimental, field centered, transactional and documental design, authors like Duffuaa, Dixon and Raouf (2005), Nava (1999) and Moubray (2000), and the Covenin 3049-93 norm were consulted. On first instance, a description to the systems associated with all twenty-five (25) vehicles in the fleet was made, allowing to design a functional and technical coding system with alphanumeric characters, as well as the development of ten (10) fact sheets, with technical information of each model in the fleet. For failure characterization, a failure modes, effects and criticality analysis was made, proving that all of the studied failures were of a chronic type. Additionally, a historical failure data was statistically analyzed, allowing to turn failure analysis parameters into reliability, availability, and maintainability calculations. Lastly, combining the failure data with manufacturer handbooks, sixty-six (66) maintenance activities were determined to prevent future failures, these were then selectively included in five (5) preventive maintenance plans, indicating frequency, duration, failure mode to prevent and responsible for executing each activity.

headline: Senior Consultant at Deloitte | Chicago Booth MBA
about:
I am currently a student at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business.  I love the challenge of stepping outside my comfort zone and expanding my horizons.  I have always enjoyed solving problems by pursing knowledge and using my analytical skillset.  I have learned from my professors and peers to ask questions and think critically.

I've built a strong foundation at the intersection of technology and consulting in the digital advertising world. During my time at The Trade Desk, I analyzed and created insights based on large data sets, consulted with clients working across a multitude of industries, and introduced clients to smarter programmatic advertising practices including data-driven targeting, multi-channel investment, and full-funnel measurement.

I graduated from University of Chicago in June 2017.  I majored in economics.  My classes were rigorous, with an emphasis on how to think, not what to think.  

My cheerfulness is one of my most prominent characteristics and the one I am most proud of.  I have been an optimist for as long as I can remember.  As I see it, the glass is always half full.

My family, my education, my athletics and my friends have been the key pillars in my life.  Through them, I have learned how important hard work, honesty, and a sense of humor are. I hope to make a relevant contribution to any organization that I am a part of utilizing the skills and talents I have honed over the years.

about:
I’m a Senior Director working in the sports business, media and marketing industry – currently shaping the sports media rights advisory business at Deloitte.

My focus today is advising our clients on how best to navigate the sports industry landscape - analysing market opportunities, identifying value, building business cases and negotiating successful commercial outcomes.

I have over 20 years’ experience within the industry itself, primarily acquiring and selling sports assets to help drive commercial returns for rights holders, agencies and broadcasters.

experience.description:
Leading the Sports Media Rights advisory business within the Sports Business Group.

My role is to help sports organisations, governing bodies, leagues, clubs, investors and broadcasters to maximise their value through media rights - providing clients with insights to help transform their business, resolve challenges and fuel opportunities for growth.

The Sports Business Group is a market-leading team of specialist advisors working exclusively on sports assignments, providing clients with specialist sports industry knowledge.

There are two Market Offerings within the Sports Business Group:

Sports Advisory
We equip our clients with world-class knowledge and insights, to seize opportunities within a rapidly evolving industry:

Establishing long-term financial sustainability. Ensuring operational excellence and robust governance models. ​

Driving transformational change. Developing and implementing industry-leading strategies.  ​

Catalysing economic and social growth. Driving the impact that sport delivers to people and place.


Sports M&A 
We identify, facilitate and execute M&A deals that propel the global sports industry forward. Our end-to-end expertise encompasses: ​

M&A strategy: We guide investors and rightsholders through the critical steps of their investment strategies, ensuring alignment with their overall objectives.​

Lead advisory: We structure and execute deals to secure optimum capital and strategic outcomes. ​

Due diligence: Our rigorous and trusted diligence process identifies key risk factors to empower informed investment decisions.

I led the acquisition of media rights for Warner Bros Discovery (WBD) across key Football properties, Rugby, Golf and other projects.

This involves acquiring rights/content for TNT Sports, Eurosport and Discovery+.

Prior to that I led the acquisitions and sales of Golf media rights across the business, managing the global sales of PGA TOUR media rights – one of the most significant projects within WBD’s international sports rights sub-licensing portfolio.

GOLFTV is a new international destination for golf fans created by Discovery, the global leader in real-life entertainment and home of the Olympics in Europe, in partnership with the PGA TOUR. The first-of-its-kind digital platform, will include a dedicated video streaming service, ensuring you can watch many of golf’s most exciting tournaments, players and moments anytime, anywhere on every screen and device. The new venture from Discovery will seek to create a worldwide home for all things golf, with new content and features added on a regular basis to build GOLFTV into the ultimate golf experience.

I led the acquisition and sales of sports media rights & digital content within the UK & Ireland, Italy and Sub-Saharan African markets for the Sportfive agency (previously Lagardere Sports).
I also led the global media rights sales process for the 2022 & 2026 Commonwealth Games and managed our global data & betting portfolio of rights.

This included working with many leading sports properties, proactively managing existing accounts and relationships, as well as driving new business with Associations, Broadcasters, Clubs and Leagues.

Furthermore, my remit extends across the wider Lagardère Sports business - working with our Digital, Consultancy, and Original Content teams to execute on new opportunities and technologies.

I worked with sports rights holders, sports federations, organising bodies, research agencies, sponsors, brands (and their agencies) to help them measure and maximise their return on investment in sport.

This included helping to improve the value of sponsor/brand advertising by providing real-time multi-channel messaging across TV/social, and supporting content owners with a technology to better identify and track their content - ultimately providing actionable insights to improve decision-making.


4C is powering the future of advertising with software that improves media planning, measurement, and buying. A data science company, 4C provides brands, agencies, networks, and operators with the world’s most comprehensive platform for social and television advertising. 4C created the first platform to enable advertising across Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, Pinterest, and Instagram through certified API access. 4C also operates Teletrax, the largest global TV monitoring network covering more than 2,100 channels in 76 countries. The company has staff in Atlanta, Chicago, Eindhoven, Hong Kong, Geneva, Los Angeles, London, Munich, New York, Portland, Pune, San Francisco, Seattle, Singapore, and Tampa. publications.publishedAt: Defense AT&L, a publication of the Defense Acquisition University · Nov 4, 2016
publications.description: Additive manufacturing, more often called "3D printing," has grown steadily in both awareness and popularity over the last decade. Is it a fad? headline: Deloitte Global Deputy CEO
about:
As Deloitte’s Global Deputy CEO, I’m responsible for driving performance and optimizing an integrated strategy across our $67 billion network of more than 460,000 professionals. My focus spans our global businesses, strategy, and our most strategic investments, including sustainability and generative AI. 

For more than 30 years, I have had the privilege of working side-by-side with clients to help them solve their most complex business challenges, always seeking innovative paths while harnessing the power of teaming and diversity of thought.  

This same passion for problem solving and the power of relationships applies to my affiliations beyond Deloitte. As a proud graduate of DePaul University, I currently serve on the Board of Trustees.  

I am also a board member of: 
• Boys & Girls Club of Chicago: an organization with a mission to enable all young people, especially those who need us most, to reach their full potential. 
• Catalyst: a global nonprofit organization that aims to create workplaces that work for women and for everyone.  
• New Profit: a philanthropic organization committed to catalyzing the impact of social entrepreneurs who are expanding access and opportunity in America. 

As a purpose-driven leader, I am passionate about mentoring and developing the next generation of leaders. 

I currently live in Chicago with my husband and two children. Outside of work, I enjoy spending time with my family and friends on the shores of Lake Michigan.

Pulse was a mobile commitment saving service that gave unbanked people a safe and convenient way to save and commit money toward smart purchases, such as healthy food, school fees, and medicine. By using simple mobile phones, a deposit system similar to mobile recharge methods, and a network of certified vendors, families could save money when and where they shop, and use that money in the future when they need it the most. 

During my tenure with Pulse, my main areas of focus were to understand customer concerns, build out the vendor agent network, conduct workshops to build a user base and collaborate with the cofounders on the overall business strategy.

receivedRecommendations.description:
Brendan brought his signature energy and positivity to Open Communities when I hired him, helping to drive the organization to a new level of broad-based advocacy. Thanks to his track record of success in tenants' rights work, including policy research on equitable inspections and transit-oriented development. I was able to raise grant funding from foundations to create a first-ever policy advocacy position for the agency, and put Brendan in charge. He ran with it. A big feather in his cap was working in coalition to pass fair housing protections in Cook County for households with vouchers. 

I remember when Brendan worked closely with the residents of a 292-unit manufactured housing community in a northern Chicago suburb as they advocated for better living conditions (including clean water), legal leases, and fair treatment by the management.  In the midst of an affluent area, that development was home to a critical mass of local low-wage multi-ethnic workers, people with disabilities, and older adults.  Brendan not only organized and advised residents, he brought local and state officials together to resolve deep-seated problems. After several years of dogged advocacy, the development got a hookup to that suburb’s water supply and the whole development was saved. Brendan would deflect compliments about what anyone would consider to be a huge victory and would give credit to the resident and political leaders.

His greatest strengths are his ability to relate to and get along with people of diverse backgrounds; energy; sense of humor; enthusiasm for housing justice and social change; strategic thinking; knowledge of fair and affordable housing; persistence; initiative; and overall leadership ability. Any organization will benefit from Brendan’s rich and varied experiences. Brendan is an asset to the community development world.

But just as importantly, Brendan is (1) deeply dedicated to dismantling systemic racism and (2) a relentless optimist. You really need both qualities to carry this work forward and he has them. I'd work with Brendan again anytime.

headline: HR Business Transformation through Technical Innovation -  Deloitte Consulting
about:
I'm passionate about realizing human potential and, somewhat ironically, believe that well-designed technology is the best way to do that. 

I have over 12 years experience in HR Business Transformation - deploying the right technology and crisp processes to provide remarkable human experiences. I’ve created and/or managed all the complex global recruiting and onboarding technical systems and processes for one of the world’s largest banks – hiring 70 thousand people a year from 1.4 million applications. 

I have led multiple HR products from concept to production. I assumed responsibility for our HR electronic forms platform after a (failed) pilot project at one work site. Under my ownership this product grew to welcome new hires globally - guiding them confidently through the process of filling and signing the bazillion forms needed before starting work for a complex global financial giant. It also saved Citi $8 million annually. And that is just one of the HR experiences I have crafted.

I achieve results through collaborative stakeholder management, Lean continuous process improvement methodology, and Agile project management principles.

Prior to finding my passion for HR, for 8 years I created data architecture and analytics to better manage business expenses through transparency and collaboration on best practices.

I enjoy working in partnership with talented people to solve difficult problems and I have a track record of delivering results.

headline: Public Sector Consultant
about: Experienced Program Manager with a demonstrated history of working in the higher education and environmental industries. Skilled in Research, Public-Private Partnerships, Policy Analysis, Nonprofit Organizations, International Relations, and Leadership. Strong professional with a Master of Public Administration (MPA) focused in Management and Policy Analysis with a focus on Environmental and Social Policy from American University.

experience.description: As a public sector strategy consultant, my goal is to help government clients achieve their missions more effectively and efficiently. I work at the intersection of strategy and implementation, providing guidance on everything from resource allocation to program evaluation. I have a proven track record of facilitating collaborative workshops, conducting comprehensive research, and preparing actionable recommendations that enable clients to make informed decisions and create lasting, positive change for the communities they serve.

In my role at Resultant, I spearheaded the operations and reporting for the public sector sales team. I developed efficient business processes that significantly improved proposal win rates and identified key market opportunities, driving substantial growth in new business. My efforts in managing a robust pipeline valued at over $100M enhanced visibility and informed strategic decision-making. I worked with executive leadership to recommend sales and contracting strategies, contributing to a 7x increase in public sector booked sales between 2020 and 2024.

During my time with Topcoder, I managed all public sector accounts, focusing especially on acquiring new clients within the federal space. As the public sector account manager, I was responsible for developing and executing comprehensive growth and success strategies. Within just six months, I closed over $1 million in booked sales and was well on my way to surpassing my sales targets. By leveraging platforms such as beta.SAM, GSA MAS, and NASA CoECI, I built a robust pipeline of public sector opportunities, significantly increasing the number of qualified leads. I led the GSA MAS submission process, where I coordinated with external consultants, oversaw compliance reviews, and managed content development, resulting in a more efficient and streamlined submission. Additionally, I trained staff on proposal methodologies, which significantly improved the quality of our proposal content, and I established a proposal process that continued to benefit Topcoder long after my tenure.

I played a central role in driving the firm’s business development and growth strategy, targeting 30% growth in the next year and positioning the company to scale from a Small Business to a competitive large business in five years. I led capture planning and managed multiple business development opportunities with senior leadership, prioritizing efforts with DHS, HHS, USDA, Commerce, and FirstNet, and managed vehicle strategies across OASIS SB, NIH BPSS, SeaPort NxG, and GSA MAS (formerly PSS and IT 70).

I independently assessed opportunities, making Go/No Go recommendations, and guided the creation of white papers and concept papers for current and prospective clients. I also led proposal development from capture through submission, supported recruiting for new projects, and improved organizational processes, including developing new tools and trainings for business development staff.

In my role as Deputy Task Lead for a pilot broadband loan and grant program at USDA, I managed a team of 7+ staff, ensuring timely and high-quality delivery work products. I streamlined the content development process and oversaw the creation of education and outreach materials across more than six topic areas including slide decks, fact sheets, and FAQs . My leadership in quality assurance and technical review elevated the consistency and impact of program materials. I also led and presented more than 25 technical assistance webinars and workshops for USDA, federal stakeholders, and the public. Additionally, I successfully supported all aspects of workshop planning and execution, including venue negotiations and logistics, contributing to the effective rollout of technical assistance and education initiatives.

I led business improvement efforts that resulted in CMMI Level 3 and ISO 9001 certifications, strengthening the organization's credibility and efficiency. I participated in eight prime and seven subcontractor bids, winning six prime bids that opened access to over $100 million in IDIQ and BPA opportunities, which generated more than $6 million in revenue. I supported the firm's sales planning and closely monitored a pipeline of 45+ leads in Hubspot CRM, working with senior leadership to drive client outreach, strategic partnerships, and competitive analysis. My efforts in identifying and qualifying new opportunities involved analytical research and relationship building across multiple sectors. I collaborated with marketing and consulting teams to create business development collateral and effective communication tools to support client engagement, and managed proposal teams of three to eight consultants to ensure workflow, compliance, and quality.

I supported two nationwide assessment reports for DHS Science & Technology, focusing on Wireless Emergency Alerting and situational awareness. My work included facilitating a 50-person workshop in the National Capital Region to identify current capabilities and gather future requirements from key stakeholders. I conducted over 40 interviews with alert originators, technologists, and social media experts, collecting data on current practices and emerging needs. I also performed comprehensive literature reviews, examining client resources, operational requirements, previous assessments, market research, After Action Reports, press releases, social media, and congressional mandates to inform recommendations for improved emergency alerting.

As Program Specialist, I managed student and volunteer engagement for the after-school tutoring and enrichment program, summer enrichment program, and Career Exploration Fair. I independently oversaw an academic support program with 100+ tutor volunteers and students and regularly collected and analyzed student performance data to propose individualized improvement plans. I represented the office at partnership meetings, delivered presentations, supported the program director with research and writing, and led the social media strategy to increase community engagement and student recruitment.
As a canvasser, I connected with community members to promote the campaign's goals, implemented grassroots organizing strategies, and helped build a strong network of local supporters.

In this role I advocated for the advancement of innovative financing and risk-sharing solutions for capital improvement projects. I independently owned the drafting and publishing of a monthly newsletter and researched, wrote, and edited case studies that delivered timely insights and best practices to members. My experience includes maintaining the member database, developing panel content for workshops, executing conferences and events, managing the organization's online presence, and distributing promotional materials. I also contributed to a key white paper advocating P3 projects as innovative funding solutions, supporting the growth of public and private sector partnerships.

As a Student Analyst with the US Government Accountability Office’s Natural Resources and Environment team, I contributed to a high profile report on environmental and scientific cooperation in the Arctic. I worked collaboratively to analyze and synthesize qualitative data, develop interview strategies, and author case studies that advanced our research. I participated in high-level interviews, including with the Governor of Alaska and Sami leadership, enriching the report’s insights and credibility. I also hosted a Russian delegation in Washington, DC, helping to strengthen our international research partnerships. By balancing multiple priorities and working closely with both local and remote team members, I consistently contributed to results that advanced our team’s mission.

More recently, my focus has been working on the latest Microsoft Technology Stack such as .Net Core, ASP.NET Core, ASP.NET Core Web Api, EF Core.

In addition, I have worked extensively on the front-end as well on Javascript, JQUERY, AJAX, HTML5, CSS3 and Bootstrap. More recently, I have had the opportunity to learn and implement modern Javascript Technology Stacks such as ReactJs, Redux and Angular.

I enjoy learning new technologies and applying them to solve business problems. 

I am open to positions which are dynamic and challenging and provide opportunities to implement cutting edge technologies to develop responsive high performing and scalable web applications.

experience.description: At Deloitte, I work as a Senior Consultant. Currently I am providing my services to a State Agency, a client of Deloitte, by modernizing a legacy application using Microsoft Technology Stack.

At JLL I am working for a project called Dealio. Dealio is a SOX compliant web based deal management application. It also handles JLL Brokers’ commissions, commission forecasting and revenue recognition. Thus, Dealio is a very critical system for JLL. As a part of Dealio modernization, I was involved in developing REST API’s using C#.Net, .Net Core, EF Core, Azure SQL, Azure APIM. These APIs were used by other systems in JLL to send information about deals and their revenue. In addition, I also developed an Azure Web Job that sends deal updates asynchronously to other JLL systems using Azure Service Bus.

Prior to working for Dealio, I was a part of the Markets team. As a part of its engineering team, I was involved in developing responsive web applications for JLL Brokers to help tenants identify and align strategic business, financial, and operational objectives with real estate requirements. These broker tools are being developed utilizing the most recent generation of cutting-edge technologies such as .NET 4.6, ASP.NET MVC 5.2, ReactJs, Redux, HTML 5, CSS3, Bootstrap 3 and SQL SERVER 2017. 

Prior to working for the Markets team, I worked in the Capital Markets group at JLL. Jones Lang LaSalle Capital Markets is a full-service global provider of capital solutions for real estate investors and occupiers. I was a part of the team that developed a tool called CapLink. CapLink is the proprietary tool of Jones Lang LaSalle Capital Markets. CapLink was developed using technologies such as .NET 4.0, ASP.NET MVC 5.0, KnockoutJs, AngularJs, CoffeeScript, HTML 5, CSS3 and SQL SERVER 2014. CapLink provides real-time market insight and tracks which lenders, buyers and sellers are most active nationally. CapLink is used for every assignment to ensure all sources are contacted and monitored to achieve the most aggressive terms.

Working for Genome International Corp, an IT Services Company based in Madison, WI. Currently working for its client JLL (Jones Lang LaSalle) as a Full Stack Senior IT Consultant. Prior to working at Jones Lang LaSalle, I worked for some reputed clients of Genome namely Greatland Corporation, Plan Administrators Inc in Green Bay Wisconsin, Wells Fargo in Minneapolis, TTX in Chicago, Electronic Theatre Controls (ETC) and Covance Inc in Madison area in Wisconsin. My work at all these companies was to provide services as consultant specializing in Microsoft Technologies and build web applications and products to increase business productivity and provide competitive advantage using cutting edge technologies.

Worked at Omni's clients in the Green Bay area, WI namely PAi (Plan Administrators Inc) and Greatland Corporation. At PAi I was part of a project called YBR. The goal of YBR  was to develop a system to administer payrolls and 401k plans utilizing the most recent generation of Microsoft Technologies.

headline: Audit & Assurance Senior Manager at Deloitte
about:
As an experienced Audit and Assurance Senior Manager at Deloitte, I specialize in providing comprehensive audit services to the financial services industry, with a particular focus on banking and insurance sectors. My expertise lies in audit innovation, robust risk assessment procedures, and the adoption of new accounting standards, all aimed at enhancing audit efficiency and effectiveness. I am passionate about creating innovative solutions that drive improved audit processes and documentation, ensuring compliance and excellence in every engagement.

Beyond my core audit role, I am engaged in advancing our firm’s culture and operations. I serve on the Central RMP Council, where I help shape regional strategies and initiatives, and I am a member of the Management Advisory Council in the office, collaborating with leadership to drive improvement and foster a positive work environment. My commitment extends to mentoring colleagues, supporting professional development, and contributing to firm-wide initiatives.

I am an actively licensed CPA and member of the ISCPA (including involvement on the Financial Institutions Committee) and AICPA.

experience.description: Seven + years of experience providing audit and assurance services primarily to financial services clients. Specializes in audit innovation, coordination of global audits, robust risk assessment procedures, agile project management, and new accounting standard adoption procedures. Created innovative solutions for improved audit processes and enhanced audit documentation that had a tangible impact on audit efficiency and effectiveness. I am a transformation coach for many engagement teams, focusing on how we leverage our audit technologies to make a more efficient audit approach and save our clients time and resources. publications.title: Predicting Hospital Readmissions from Claims Data
publications.publishedAt: Business Intelligence and Analytics for Heathcare Conference · Jul 1, 2011
publications.description: We created an in-patient readmission predictive model, using data mining methods, to predict the likelihood of urgent or emergency in-patient readmission for a given patient within certain period of discharge from an in-patient facility. The model outputs the likelihood of readmission and the key factors that influenced the decision. The model minimally requires either claims data or electronic medical records.  Model performance is higher if prescription data or external socio-economic data is available. The clinical history and prescription history can be derived either from claims or from electronic medical records.  The readmission likelihood, along with reasons for readmission, could be used for tailoring a better discharge plan or for assignment of a member to a complex case management program.

projects.title: Research Article: Gold Digging and Emotional Labour in Relationships
projects.description:
This paper explores the concept of emotion work or emotional labour in the personal sphere in general
and within the context of heterosexual relationships and marriages in particular. It further examines the
role of gender and attempts to draw comparisons between the emotional labour required for jobs and the emotional work required to sustain a heterosexual marriage or relationship. It inspects the narrative of a ‘gold digging’ spouse during divorce settlements, and the harm that it inflicts on the non-propertied spouse.

projects.title: Research Paper: Effect of Political Instability on Economic Growth
projects.description:
The purpose of this paper is to empirically determine the effects of political instability
on economic growth. We look at how political instability affects the different
variables affecting economic growth and we explore the question of whether political
stability can sometimes hamper economic growth. Theories indicating a positive
relationship between political instability and higher economic growth have been
included to provide a fuller picture. We end with a case study of the current economic
and political scenario of India and examine it through the lens of political stability.

projects.title: SB COP30
projects.description:
SB COP30 is a landmark private-sector initiative led by Ricardo Mussa and the Brazilian National Confederation of Industry (CNI), created to elevate the role of business leadership in the COP30 climate negotiations, which will take place in Belém, Brazil, in 2025.

Inspired by the B20 model (business engagement platform of the G20), SB COP30 brings together Brazilian and global companies to propose practical solutions and strategic recommendations that support climate goals while advancing economic development. The initiative aims to show that it is possible to decarbonize while ensuring energy and food security, competitiveness, and efficiency.

SB COP30 is structured around eight thematic working groups, each led by C-level executives from major corporations:
	•	Energy Transition – Daniela Manique (Solvay-Rhodia)
	•	Circular Economy & Materials – Tércio Borlenghi (Ambipar)
	•	Bioeconomy – João Paulo Ferreira (Natura)
	•	Food Systems – Gilberto Tomazoni (JBS)
	•	Green Jobs & Skills – Rafael Segrera (Schneider Electric)
	•	Climate Finance – Luciana Ribeiro (eB Capital)
	•	Sustainable & Resilient Cities – Rubens Menin (MRV)
	•	Nature-based Solutions – Marcelo Medeiros (re.green)

Each group will deliver up to three key recommendations to the Brazilian presidency of COP30 and global stakeholders, shaping discussions and influencing outcomes at the conference.

SB COP30 reflects a bold vision: to establish a permanent platform for business engagement in the global climate agenda, led by Brazil but connected to the world. It reinforces the private sector’s role in delivering scalable, impactful, and science-based climate solutions.

I have the honor to lead as a knowledge partner the Sustainable Cities and Green jobs/skills thematics.

headline: US Chief Growth Officer at Deloitte
about:
As a US Chief Growth Officer at Deloitte, I’m responsible for driving growth across our businesses. My background and experience has allowed me to develop a unique blend of skills as an advisor, team champion, community builder, and strategist, all of which I bring to this role. My focus is on applying Deloitte’s vast capabilities to the market, building profitable, scalable business practices, and deepening client relationships. 
  
Throughout my time as a partner in Deloitte & Touche LLP, I've focused on providing integrated services to our clients across the entire value chain. In my previous roles, I also served as the US Clients, Industries & Insights Leader for Deloitte and led the US Consumer industry.  
  
With over 28 years of experience working with both publicly and privately held clients across multiple consumer and industrial products sectors, my focus is also on navigating challenges like new product and service innovation, talent shortages, changing trade and regulatory environments, as well as adapting to new business models. I’m passionate about creating authentic, high-performing teams - empowering those around me to reach their full potential and live boldly. 
  
A big part of my story is rooted in my Indian heritage. As a first-gen American raised by a single mom with no formal education, I’m incredibly grateful to be living my dreams. My upbringing has deeply influenced the causes and organizations I support. I’ve been privileged to serve on the board of directors for the National Association of Manufacturers and as vice chair of The Manufacturing Institute’s STEP Ahead Initiative.  
  
I am also on Deloitte's management committee, actively involved in the Chicago community - serving as a board member for Chicago Scholars Foundation and Leadership Greater Chicago, helping to develop emerging leaders. 
  
I hold a degree in Accounting from NIU and am a proud member of the American Institute of CPAs. 
  
A few fun facts about me: 
• I attended NIU, initially dreaming of studying sharks (my favorite animal!) and curing cancer, but eventually discovering my passion for business and accounting. 
• I met Cal Ripken Jr. in 1983 after his World Series win (I once aspired to be the first female MLB player) and years later, it came full circle when I interviewed him at Deloitte. 
• I love historical fiction—I enjoy not only escaping but also learning something new.

I work in subject areas ranging from accounting for income taxes, tax compliance, domestic and international acquisitions and restructurings, and tax planning matters. My goal is to bring a hands-on and practical approach to driving an effective tax function. 

I am excited about the impact of Transformation and Innovation on our profession and our careers. I seek new ways to solve challenging tax issues for both our clients and our firm. I previously established and led Deloitte’s Tax Analytics Insights practice, enabling clients’ use of analytics to change the way tax departments are managed.  

I was the former leader of Deloitte’s US Inbound tax practice. Increasing access to the accounting field for more professionals and future leaders is a passion of mine. I'm involved with Deloitte's MADE commitment, Making Accounting Diverse & Equitable, and other areas of our Diversity, Equity & Inclusion efforts.

I am active in the nonprofit community, serving on the Boards for the Southern Illinois University Foundation, the Pontikes Center for Advanced Analytics and Artificial Intelligence, and the University of Illinois-Deloitte Foundation Center for Business Analytics. publications.title: Tax Policy and Heterogeneous Investment Behavior
publications.description: We estimate the effect of temporary tax incentives on equipment investment using shifts in accelerated depreciation. Analyzing data for over 120,000 firms, we present three findings. First, bonus depreciation raised investment in eligible capital relative to ineligible capital by 10.4 percent between 2001 and 2004 and by 16.9 percent between 2008 and 2010. Second, small firms respond 95 percent more than big firms. Third, firms respond strongly when the policy generates immediate cash flows, but not when cash flows only come in the future. This heterogeneity materially affects  investment-weighted estimates and supports models in which financial frictions or fixed costs  amplify investment responses.

headline: Finance Transformation Consulting | Senior Manager
about:
As an experienced Senior Manager in Deloitte's Finance Transformation practice, I help Fortune 500 organizations develop and execute strategies. My work spans technology-enabled programs, M&A integrations and separations, FP&A and Performance Management process improvements, and value capture initiatives.

With a strong foundation in strategy and operations, I’ve honed my skills across management consulting (Deloitte Consulting), corporate finance (General Electric), and dynamic start-up environments (Weavr.io). My focus lies within the office of the CFO, where I advise on a wide range of topics, including planning and management process improvement, turning strategies into actionable delivery roadmaps, and driving project delivery across technology and process modernization.

I have a particular passion for the life sciences and healthcare industry, where I believe in leveraging technology to democratize access to quality healthcare at an affordable price. Helping patients reach their health goals and improve outcomes is a driving force behind my work.

Additionally, I'm deeply committed to the safe usage and application of AI, not only as a tool for the finance function but as a broader value creator for individuals, businesses, and society. Through automation and insights generation, I see AI as a transformative technology that can unlock new opportunities and efficiencies.

Finally, as a global-minded and collaborative leader, I've had the privilege of working across the US, Kenya, and the UK, bringing diverse perspectives to my work. I hold an MBA from London Business School (2021) and a BS from the Kelley School of Business (2013).
